definition: Construe means to interpret the meaning of something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word construe. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know construe should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The neighbors construed the half-finished fence as a property claim, though the builder had simply run out of lumber.
To read a note is lighter than to construe it — reading takes the words in, while construing works out what they are really meant to do.
Decipher goes further than construe: construing untangles ambiguous meaning, but deciphering cracks meaning that is hidden or garbled on purpose.

Interpret is the plain, broad word for making sense of anything — a poem, a statute, a shrug. Construe narrows it: the careful, often disputed reading of particular words or acts, usually in the frame 'construe something as something.' Every construal is an interpretation; not every interpretation is a construal.

Decode works out meaning that was deliberately hidden — a cipher, a scrambled signal, slang built to keep outsiders out. Construe untangles meaning that is open but ambiguous: the words sit in plain sight, and the work is deciding what they were meant to do.

To parse a sentence is to take it apart — identify its grammar, its parts, how the pieces connect. Construe goes past structure to intent: what the words, once parsed, were actually meant to do. You can parse a line perfectly and still not know how to construe it.

When the composer marked the finale only “with fire,” every conductor construed the phrase differently: one took it as speed, another as fury, a third as brightness — three performances grown from the same two words.
Construe is more exact than interpret because the puzzle is the meaning of particular words — ambiguous ones, read closely and defensibly, often as one thing or another.
And mind the sound-alike trap: construe means to read meaning out of something, while construct means to build; the two share a Latin root and little else today.

Construe is precise where interpret is broad: it suits the careful, often disputed reading of particular words or acts, and it usually appears in the frame “construe something as something.” Contextualize, its neighbor in this unit, does different work — it supplies the surroundings; construe extracts the meaning.

The sign at the park gate says only: 'No vehicles beyond this point.' For years nobody thought twice about it.
Cars stayed out, and that seemed to be the whole story.
Then a ten-year-old rode her electric scooter down the main path, and the parks board discovered how much work five words can refuse to do.
Each camp construed the rule to fit its own picture of what the sign was for.
Safety-minded neighbors read 'vehicle' as anything with wheels and a motor; parents of scooter kids read it as cars and trucks, full stop.
The board finally voted to list examples on the sign itself -- an admission that words left open will be read, and read again, until someone narrows them.
